summary: E2E validation of the new GitHub Bulk Revoke admin tool (backend + UI). Created 7-test pytest file exercising GET /admin/github/connections shape+live_verified flag, POST /admin/github/bulk-revoke dry_run preview (no side effects) and 403 live_verification_pending gate, and POST /admin/github/flag-idle non-destructive path. 6 passed / 1 skipped (hard_guard_blocked path could not be triggered because the current preview DB has 0 installations with pat_status=='valid' — both installations have pat_status='missing'; unit tests already cover the hard-guard branch with mocked data). Playwright UI verify against real preview confirmed: page renders, amber 'Live verification pending' banner shown, all data-testids present, view filters work (revokable=2, all=2, idle=0), 'Revoke selected…' button is disabled (playwright reports element is not enabled and modal does NOT open on click), select-all limited to visible/filtered rows (2/2), and Flag Idle button remains usable. Regression tests test_github_app_router.py + test_github_app_service.py: 48 passed, 2 failed — both are the pre-existing TestCallback::test_replayed_state_soft_redirect / test_expired_state_soft_redirect the founder explicitly called out as unrelated. BIN Tracker smoke: /admin/bin/{bin_id}/projects still routes (returns 404 BIN not found as expected).
critical_code_review_comments: routers/admin_bin.py is now 913 lines — still under the 1000-line refactor threshold but drifting; consider splitting Section 1b into a dedicated routers/admin_github_bulk_revoke.py in a future iteration.

In /admin/github/bulk-revoke, the hard-guard (400) is evaluated BEFORE the feature-flag gate (403). This is correct for UX (user sees the more actionable message first), but note that a caller sending confirm_text='REVOKE' with a purely-revokable selection today would get 403; a caller with valid rows and no confirm gets 400 regardless of flag state. Documented, no fix needed.

Bulk-revoke rate limit is keyed only on admin identity + action; multiple concurrent admins are unaffected which is fine, but a burst from one admin retrying after a 429 could still race with an in-flight batch. Not a correctness bug for this feature; note for future.
